name: Herald Nullmark
description: Herald Nullmark is a tiny barren body, barely qualifying as a dwarf planet, orbiting in the outer reaches of a system that has seen better days. Its surface is a monotony of grey regolith pockmarked by impact craters, the largest of which spans nearly a quarter of the body's diameter. Solar wind has stripped the exposed rock to a polished smoothness in places, while shadowed craters hold regolith that has not been disturbed in millions of years.

The gravity is so weak that a strong jump could achieve escape velocity, and the surface clings to its dust through habit more than force. There is nothing here: no air, no water, no geological interest, no reason to visit. The body orbits in silence, turning slowly in the weak light of a distant sun, its surface temperature ranging from moderate heat to bitter cold as it rotates. It is a world defined by absence.

A graveyard of decommissioned satellites orbits Herald Nullmark, placed here because the body's negligible gravity and remote location make it a convenient disposal site. The satellites span decades of technology and multiple organizations, their orbits slowly decaying as the body's feeble gravity pulls them into eventual impact. Among the decommissioned hardware, several satellites of unknown origin maintain stable orbits that should have decayed long ago, their power systems apparently still functional.

Herald Nullmark has no value except as a disposal site, a status that makes the functional satellites all the more anomalous. Their designs match no known manufacturer, and their continued operation suggests either remarkable engineering or active maintenance by unknown parties. The body itself is unremarkable, but it has become a waypoint for those investigating the unknown satellites, a null space that has acquired significance through proximity to a mystery it did not create.
